thread:
alex: Heads-up — Delta Labs POC is hitting intermittent 429s when they ramp to ~120 qps. Also they asked about enterprise pricing for dedicated capacity and want to finish the security questionnaire today. Can we spin up a war-room? cc @maria @samir

maria: On it. Can you paste the exact error payload and the request id? Also which model and region?

alex: here's a sample of the client error:
```json
{"error":"rate_limited","message":"429 Too Many Requests","request_id":"req_0a9f3b"}
```
They call our hosted API, model: redwood-13b-v2, region: us-east-1. Traffic pattern: many short chats with streaming responses.

samir: Likely hitting the per-account token QPS throttle. Do we have their API key mapped to any quota overrides? @jess can you cross-check Dedicated vs Hosted quota?

jess: Checking now. Delta Labs is on trial hosted account with default burst limit 100 rps and steady 60 rps. They spiked to 120 rps during warmup. I can bump burst to 200 for 2 hours. Need approval from sales-ops for billing implications.

sales-ops: Approve temporary burst bump (2h). Track usage and warn if sustained >80% of bumped limit. Also share rough pricing delta per hour.

alex: Thanks. On SSQ — they returned SAQ sections incomplete; they need clarification on our data retention and network controls. I have the SSQ PDF attached in thread (not included here).

olivia: For SSQ: short answers — 'we retain request logs for 30 days by default, can extend with enterprise plan', 'VPC Private offers no egress to internet', 'we support KMS/HSM'. I'll draft responses.

samir: Dev runtime — if they get 429 fallback should route to smaller model variant (redwood-7b-quant) to keep latency. But note semantics degrade. We can set routing policy to fallback automatically. Who can apply that config?

jess: I can add a route with fallback and a lower token cap in console. Need to coordinate while I apply so we don't interrupt active sessions. ETA 10m.

alex: Posting curl they used:
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
 -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
 -d '{"model":"redwood-13b-v2","input":"...","stream":true}'
```
They use streaming, which increases connection count.

deploy-bot: ecs/service/redwood-hosted-api: rolling update started by jess (task group srv-frontend).

maria: Quick triage steps: 1) Bump burst (jess) 2) Add routing fallback (jess) 3) Re-run their warmup with controlled ramp 4) Send SSQ answers (olivia) 5) If still failing escalate to eng-runtime. Who owns escalation?

samir: I'll own eng-runtime escalation if changes don't help within 30m. Please add logs with request_id 'req_0a9f3b' and timestamp 2026-03-21T15:04:12Z.

alex: I'll ask Delta to repro at 15:25 UTC and share logs. Also they asked for enterprise pricing per-seat vs committed GPU pricing. @sales-ops can you draft two options?

sales-ops: Drafted in comments: (1) pay-as-you-go hosted — $X/1M tokens; (2) Dedicated reserved — $Y/month for N GPUs incl committed throughput. I'll DM full sheet.

jess: Bump applied. Burst to 200 rps for Delta Labs — expires in 2h. Routing fallback configured to redwood-7b-quant for 13b failures. Please confirm repro.

alex: Delta LABS did repro at 15:27 UTC — no 429s for 15m, but a few degraded outputs (length/truncation). They confirm streaming sessions remained stable. Good initial win. Continuing SSQ.

olivia: SSQ answers drafted and uploaded to their portal. Marking as done for now.

samir: Marking eng-runtime standdown. If anything else, open new thread and tag me. For handoff to enterprise team: @jess please include config changes in the POC runbook.

jess: Added section in runbook: burst bump, fallback routing, observations. File: //docs/pocs/delta-labs-runbook.md

alex: Thanks everyone — closing this war-room. I'll update the customer and set up follow-up for pricing next week. :thumbsup:
